sentences.text:
Sk. Nuruddin vs Unknown on 25 March, 2026
59. 25.03.2026
Court
No.8 (Tanmoy)
 In The High Court At Calcutta
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION  IA NO: CRAN/2/2026  In  CRA (DB)/248/2025  In Re: - Applications under Section 389(1) of Cr.PC, 1973 /

Section 430(1) of BNSS, 2023, in connection with the judgment  and order dated 04.04.2025, passed by the learned Additional  Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Malda, in SC No. 86/2013.
 AND  In the matter of: - SK. NURUDDIN  ...applicant/appellant.

Mr. Abhinaba Dan  ...for the applicant/appellant  Ms. Amita Gaur, Sr. Govt. Adv.
 Ms. Rajnandini Das  ...for the State  Dictated by Apurba Sinha Ray, J.
1.
Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.

Although the unnatural death was as a result of suicide committed by the victim herself,
there is no ingredient of offences punishable under Section 304B/498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.
The witnesses saw that the victim committed suicide but the post mortem report discloses that the death was due to effect of strangulation, ante mortem in nature.
All the other accused persons who were named in the First Information Report (FIR), were acquitted but the present applicant being the husband was convicted under Sections 304B/498A IPC.
He is in custody for about one year 10 months as would appear from the custody report filed by the State in Court today.
Let the report be kept on record.
2. Learned Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for suspension of sentence.

According to her,
there are sufficient incriminating materials against the applicant.
The unnatural death of the victim was caused within two years of her marriage.
The post mortem report shows that the death was caused due to strangulation.
The dead body of the victim was found in the house of the applicant but he did not provide any explanation under Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act.
3. We have considered the materials on record.

There are sufficient incriminating evidence against the present applicant that unnatural death of the applicant's wife took place in the house of the Sk. Nuruddin vs Unknown on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122359124/
1 applicant.
The applicant was unable to give explanation under Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act as to how the unnatural death of his wife occurred in the precincts of his house.
4. In view of the above, we are not inclined to extend the privilege of suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant.
5. The application being IA No: CRAN/2/2026 is accordingly dismissed.

From a departmental note dated February 25, 2026, we see that the department has received the Trial Court Records (TCRs).
7.
The department shall expedite the process of preparation of paper book and ensure that paper book is made ready by the end of May, 2026.

8. Place the appeal for final hearing in the Combined Monthly list of June, 2026.
9.
Criminal Section is directed to make available certified copies of this order to the parties, if applied for, upon compliance with all requisite formalities.

(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.) (Arijit Banerjee, J.)
